seo.meta_title: 피땀 Meaning | Hard-Earned in Korean, from BTS' Blood Sweat & Tears
seo.meta_description: AI reads 피땀 literally, so 피땀 흘려 번 돈 sounds violent. It means hard-earned money. How Koreans use 피땀 about work and parents.

ai_failure.situation: An older relative says 이거 다 피땀 흘려 번 돈이야, and you run it through an AI translator.
ai_failure.ai_mistake: Translates it word for word as 'This is money earned by shedding blood and sweat', which sounds violent or medical.
ai_failure.why_it_fails: 피땀 is one fixed word for exhausting effort. 피땀 흘려 번 돈 simply means money earned the hard way. The same image is in BTS's 2016 song title 피 땀 눈물.

natural_solution.rule: Read 피땀 as 'hard work' or 'everything someone put in', never literally.

alternatives.context: 'It's hard-earned money' — often a reason not to waste it
'My parents' hard work paid for my college'

nuance: English has 'blood, sweat and tears', but Korean 피땀 is an everyday word, not a dramatic phrase. You'll hear it most about money: parents' earnings, savings, a small business. Saying someone wasted your 피땀 is a serious complaint.
